Load the libraries/packages
```{python}
# Packages required: pandas, numpy, scipy, nfl_data_py, great_tables, matplotlib, seaborn
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import nfl_data_py as nfl
from scipy import stats
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from great_tables import GT


# Set pandas options to display numbers clearly without scientific notation
pd.set_option('display.float_format', lambda x: '%.4f' % x)
```

Let's get the most recent four season
```{python}
# Fetch 2022 through 2025 regular season play-by-play data
seasons_vector = [2022, 2023, 2024, 2025]

pbp_multi_raw = nfl.import_pbp_data(seasons_vector)

pbp_multi = pbp_multi_raw[
    (pbp_multi_raw['season_type'] == 'REG') &
    (pbp_multi_raw['posteam'].notna()) &
    ((pbp_multi_raw['play_type'].isin(['pass', 'run'])) | (pbp_multi_raw['pass'] == 1) | (pbp_multi_raw['rush'] == 1)) &
    (pbp_multi_raw['epa'].notna())
].copy()

# Display dataset size across all 4 seasons
print(f"Total analyzed scrimmage plays (2022–2025): {len(pbp_multi)}")
```

```{python}
# Weekly Offensive Metrics
weekly_offense = (
    pbp_multi.groupby(['season', 'week', 'posteam'])
    .apply(
        lambda x: pd.Series({
            'off_plays': len(x),
            'off_epa_per_play': x['epa'].mean(),
            'off_pass_epa': x.loc[x['pass'] == 1, 'epa'].mean(),
            'off_rush_epa': x.loc[x['rush'] == 1, 'epa'].mean(),
            'off_success_rate': x['success'].mean(),
            'pass_rate': (x['pass'] == 1).mean(),
            'complete_pass_pct': x['complete_pass'].mean()
        }),
        include_groups=False
    )
    .reset_index()
)

# Weekly Defensive Metrics
weekly_defense = (
    pbp_multi.groupby(['season', 'week', 'defteam'])
    .agg(
        def_plays=('epa', 'count'),
        def_epa_allowed=('epa', 'mean'),
        def_success_rate_allowed=('success', 'mean')
    )
    .reset_index()
)

# Master Panel Dataset (Weekly Team Summary)
weekly_team_panel = (
    pd.merge(
        weekly_offense,
        weekly_defense,
        left_on=['season', 'week', 'posteam'],
        right_on=['season', 'week', 'defteam']
    )
    .rename(columns={'posteam': 'team'})
    .drop(columns=['defteam'])
    .sort_values(by=['team', 'season', 'week'])
)
```


```{python}
# Preview first 10 rows of weekly panel data
weekly_team_panel.head(10)
```

Next we are going to break the data into half seasons at week 9:

```{python}
weekly_team_panel['half_season'] = np.where(weekly_team_panel['week'] <= 9, "H1", "H2")

halfseason_team_panel = (
    weekly_team_panel.groupby(['season', 'team', 'half_season'])
    .agg(
        mean_off_plays=('off_plays', 'mean'),
        mean_off_epa_per_play=('off_epa_per_play', 'mean'),
        mean_off_pass_epa=('off_pass_epa', 'mean'),
        mean_off_rush_epa=('off_rush_epa', 'mean'),
        mean_off_success_rate=('off_success_rate', 'mean'),
        mean_pass_rate=('pass_rate', 'mean'),
        mean_complete_pass_pct=('complete_pass_pct', 'mean'),
        mean_def_plays=('def_plays', 'mean'),
        mean_def_epa_allowed=('def_epa_allowed', 'mean'),
        mean_def_success_rate_allowed=('def_success_rate_allowed', 'mean')
    )
    .reset_index()
)
```

We'll start by doing just the 2025 season and running some correlations.

```{python}
# Get just the 2025 NFL play-by-play data
pbp_raw = pbp_multi[(pbp_multi['season'])==2025]

# Filter to regular season scrimmage plays
pbp_clean = pbp_raw[
    (pbp_raw['season_type'] == 'REG') &
    (pbp_raw['play'] == 1) &
    (pbp_raw['epa'].notna()) &
    (pbp_raw['posteam'].notna()) &
    (pbp_raw['play_type'].isin(['pass', 'run']))
].copy()

# Add indicators
pbp_clean['half_season'] = np.where(pbp_clean['week'] <= 9, "H1", "H2")
pbp_clean['is_explosive'] = np.where(pbp_clean['yards_gained'] >= 15, 1, 0)
pbp_clean['is_success'] = np.where(pbp_clean['epa'] > 0, 1, 0)
pbp_clean['turnover'] = ((pbp_clean['interception'] == 1) | (pbp_clean['fumble_lost'] == 1)).astype(int)
```


Turn the play-by-play data into drive-level data:
```{python}

# Drive-Level Metrics (drive_epa, turnovers_per_drive)
drive_game = (
    pbp_clean.groupby(['game_id', 'drive', 'posteam', 'half_season'])
    .agg(
        drive_total_epa=('epa', 'sum'),
        drive_turnovers=('turnover', 'sum')
    )
    .reset_index()
)

drive_summary = (
    drive_game.groupby(['posteam', 'half_season'])
    .agg(
        drive_epa=('drive_total_epa', 'mean'),
        turnovers_per_drive=('drive_turnovers', 'mean')
    )
    .reset_index()
)

# Play-Level Metrics
play_summary = (
    pbp_clean.groupby(['posteam', 'half_season'])
    .apply(
        lambda x: pd.Series({
            'mean_epa': x['epa'].mean(),
            'success_rate': x['is_success'].mean(),
            'pass_epa': x.loc[x['play_type'] == 'pass', 'epa'].mean(),
            'rush_epa': x.loc[x['play_type'] == 'run', 'epa'].mean(),
            'yards_per_play': x['yards_gained'].mean(),
            'completion_pct': x.loc[x['pass_attempt'] == 1, 'complete_pass'].mean()
        }),
        include_groups=False
    )
    .reset_index()
)

# Combine metrics
metrics_combined = pd.merge(play_summary, drive_summary, on=['posteam', 'half_season'])
metrics_combined.head()
```


Reshape the data to calculate split-half correlations:

```{python}
# Pivot to wide format: metric_H1 vs metric_H2
metrics_wide = metrics_combined.pivot(index='posteam', columns='half_season')
metrics_wide.columns = [f"{val}_{stat}" for val, stat in metrics_wide.columns]
metrics_wide = metrics_wide.reset_index()

metric_list = [
    "mean_epa", "success_rate", "pass_epa", "rush_epa",
    "yards_per_play", "drive_epa", "completion_pct", "turnovers_per_drive"
]
```
Next calculate the correlations between the first half and the second half

```{python}
# Compute Pearson r, p-value, and R-squared
corr_data = []

for m in metric_list:
    col_h1 = f"{m}_H1"
    col_h2 = f"{m}_H2"
    
    valid_data = metrics_wide[[col_h1, col_h2]].dropna()
    r, p_val = stats.pearsonr(valid_data[col_h1], valid_data[col_h2])
    
    corr_data.append({
        'metric': m,
        'r': r,
        'p_value': p_val,
        'r_squared': r ** 2
    })

correlation_results = pd.DataFrame(corr_data).sort_values(by='r', ascending=False)
```


```{python}
# Render Summary Table using Great Tables
GT(correlation_results).tab_header(
    title="2025 NFL Offense Split-Half Reliability",
    subtitle="Pearson Correlation (r) between Weeks 1-9 (H1) and Weeks 10-18 (H2)"
).cols_label(
    metric="Offensive Metric",
    r="Pearson r",
    p_value="p-value",
    r_squared="R²"
).fmt_number(
    columns=["r", "p_value", "r_squared"], 
    decimals=3
)
```



```{python}
# Visualization
plt.figure(figsize=(9, 5))
ax = sns.barplot(
    data=correlation_results,
    x='r',
    y='metric',
    palette='mako',
    hue='r',
    legend=False
)

for p in ax.patches:
    width = p.get_width()
    ax.annotate(
        f"r = {width:.2f}",
        (width, p.get_y() + p.get_height() / 2.),
        ha='left', va='center',
        xytext=(5, 0),
        textcoords='offset points',
        fontsize=10
    )

plt.xlim(-0.2, 1.0)
plt.title("Metric Repeatability: H1 vs H2 (2025 NFL Season)", fontsize=13)
plt.xlabel("Split-Half Pearson Correlation (r)")
plt.ylabel("Offensive Metric")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
